headline: Nursing Jobs in Australia: 2026 Requirements Guide

sections.title: Who Can Work as a Nurse in Australia
sections.content:
To work as a registered nurse in Australia, candidates must hold registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia through AHPRA, the national regulator. Applicants need a recognised nursing qualification, usually a bachelor's degree, and must demonstrate recent clinical practice, good character and professional indemnity arrangements.

Internationally qualified nurses must have their education and experience assessed, and many complete an approved bridging or adaptation program before gaining full registration. Enrolled nurses, who work under registered nurses, follow a separate registration pathway with a diploma-level qualification.

sections.title: English and Registration Requirements
sections.content:
All applicants must meet the Board's English language standard, commonly proven through IELTS, OET, PTE Academic or TOEFL, with minimum scores set for each test. Candidates educated in certain English-speaking countries may be exempt, but most international applicants should plan for a formal English test early.

The registration process also requires identity documents, qualification transcripts, employment references, criminal history checks and, in some cases, a skills assessment. Processing times vary, so applicants should apply several months before their planned move and keep certified copies of every document.

sections.title: Visas for International Nurses
sections.content:
Registered nurses are on Australia's skilled occupation lists, which opens several visa routes, including employer-sponsored visas and state-nominated skilled visas. The Skills in Demand visa and the Employer Nomination Scheme are the most common employer routes, while points-tested skilled visas suit candidates with strong English and experience.

Many hospitals and aged-care providers sponsor overseas nurses and help with relocation, licensing costs and settlement support. Regional employers often offer additional incentives, and working in a designated regional area can also improve the pathway to permanent residency.

sections.title: Salaries, Demand and How to Apply
sections.content:
Registered nurses in Australia typically earn between eighty-five thousand and one hundred and twenty thousand Australian dollars per year, depending on state, experience, shift loadings and overtime. Penalty rates for nights, weekends and public holidays can raise total earnings substantially above the base salary.

Demand remains strong in hospitals, aged care, community health and rural services, with shortages reported across most states. Candidates should apply directly to health services, through state health job boards or with specialist healthcare recruiters, and prepare for interviews covering clinical scenarios and patient safety.

faqs.a: You must apply for registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia through AHPRA, providing your qualification, transcripts, employment history, identity documents and criminal history checks. Internationally qualified nurses may also need a skills assessment or an approved bridging program before gaining full registration.
